module: First steps and a safe learning workspace
title: Create a backup file or verify restoration?
goal: Dump your training infobase and verify a separate restoration while preserving original work.

prerequisites.text: Your own training infobase; be able to close and reopen its modes one at a time.
Know how to create a separate folder for a backup.

sections.title: A familiar situation and a checkable question
paragraphs: A .dt file exists. Will it open as the saved infobase? Check the separate steps: load into a new empty target, observe it and return to the original.

sections.title: Which program to use
paragraphs: Perform actions in the program named at the start of each step. Nexus shows the lesson and can store an optional note. Designer and 1C:Enterprise belong to installed 1C. We are studying an empty infobase; no programming or ready-made service desk is needed.
If a suitable lawful installation already works, do not reinstall it to match an image. Begin with a separate own training infobase; use no work data or somebody else’s startup entries.

sections.title: Isolation starts with the path
paragraphs: A learning infobase needs its own directory and a clear name. Do not select an arbitrary infobase from a shared list. Before creating it, verify that the target directory is new and the source work remains intact. Never restore over an existing infobase. Isolation protects working data from learning mistakes and makes the experiment repeatable.

Use the startup window to add your own new infobase without a configuration. Empty state is expected in A1. The author’s technical experiment also creates a separate empty infobase and checks a DT restore, without loading a ready-made service desk or BSL. Creating the infobase does not create customers, requests or a service application.

A learner has at least two different results: configuration and records in installed 1C, plus completion marks and notes in Nexus. Backing up one does not transfer the other. An infobase dump file, .dt, restores the 1C infobase; it is not a certificate and contains no Nexus course progress. Saving source in Studio is not a complete infobase backup either.

sections.title: Reason through the actions before clicking
paragraphs: Restoration targets a new location. The dump links it to its source, while a clear startup-entry name and verified directory identify the correct target before launch.
First name the window, object and expected change. An illustrative model supports reasoning; it does not mean records already exist in your infobase.

sections.title: Know what a copy preserves
paragraphs: Configuration sources describe structure and code. They do not back up particular customers or documents. An infobase dump transfers its state, but usefulness is established by restoring elsewhere and inspecting the result. A file with the expected extension is weak evidence by itself.

Copying an active file infobase can capture inconsistent state. Close sessions first and follow the official dump/restore workflow. Do not keep Designer and a training-edition user session open together because the edition allows only one session. Preserve earlier attempts: a new test should not destroy evidence of the previous failure.

Give each dump a new descriptive name with a date or purpose. For example, Before_01.dt and After_02.dt are different files. A file’s existence does not prove that it can be restored. Test it by loading a specifically created empty infobase and comparing expected objects and records. The original remains unchanged during this experiment.

sections.title: Your prediction
paragraphs: Only a .cf remains instead of a .dt. Will it automatically restore particular customers?

reveal.title: Check the explanation
paragraphs: No. A CF describes the configuration. Records need an appropriate backup whose usability is checked by restoring. The A1 infobase is still empty, so this experiment does not establish customer-record transfer.

sections.title: Copying between trajectories
paragraphs: Moving from A to P creates new work with a new ID and source provenance. Content may be copied, but completion, test results and assessment from the source trajectory are not awarded. The candidate applies this mechanism only to local learning notes; an actual infobase must be copied separately with official tools.

Record source course, target course, new ID, date and synthetic-data status. Edit the new note and reopen the source. If the original text also changes, you have shared a reference or overwritten it rather than making an independent copy. The software model needs a deep copy; infobase work needs a separate restore destination.

A .cf configuration file and a .dt infobase dump serve different purposes. Type definitions without user records do not replace a data backup. Use the infobase dump command in Designer’s Administration menu for this lesson. Our empty infobase has no customer records yet: expect to restore an empty training application, not to acquire completed course examples.

sections.title: Landmarks while acting
paragraphs: Trace the transitions and name what changes at each step. This diagram explains; it neither creates an infobase nor operates installed 1C.

sections.title: Check another explanation
paragraphs: Before loading, check which startup entry and directory you selected. If the target is uncertain, cancel and return to the list. Source and copy can share the same window title. A destructive load is not needed to test this mistake.
Check the task and command name. Saving the configuration definition does not promise preservation of customer records.

sections.title: Acceptance and its limits
paragraphs: A1 acceptance includes explaining layers, modes and objects, a navigation protocol, a separate infobase and evidence that the source survives. Nexus completion is learner self-report, not a protected exam. Author automation demonstrates a particular probe on a specified version, not a learner’s personal performance.

Without the official platform, theory, diagrams, questions and notes remain available offline. Leave the native lab unattested. You may enter P1 directly: A is not a mandatory prerequisite for P. Before continuing, preserve the environment record, control results and explicitly untested items.

Finish by reopening the original and checking that you did not accidentally continue work in the copy. Give the copy its own visible startup name. For later experiments, record which work it came from and why it was created. A short human-readable note is enough; a complex JSON protocol is not a beginner prerequisite. Keep a failed attempt alongside its correction when it explains your conclusion.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: For your independent check create another empty target with a separate clear name and directory. Record source and target before loading. If the target is the source directory, cancel before loading. Restore your DT only into the new target and return to the original. State separately that empty state was checked; Nexus progress and customer records were not transferred.
Record your prediction before acting. Reveal the reference after your attempt; it explains reasoning and does not replace your own note.

steps.action: Close your own application sessions. Save intended configuration edits and update the database configuration normally. In the startup list select the original training entry and verify its directory before opening Designer. The Designer title can display the configuration name rather than the startup entry name.
steps.why: Back up an identifiable saved state rather than unsaved editor text.
steps.expected: The intended source is selected and no other session of your own remains open.

steps.action: Choose a new directory for your training backups. Give the .dt file a new name, such as Service_desk_before_01.dt. Confirm and wait for the normal completion message.
steps.why: This command saves the infobase rather than only its configuration definition.
steps.expected: A separate .dt file exists and the operation has finished.

steps.action: Close the source Designer. Create an infobase without a configuration in a new empty folder and name its startup entry “Service desk — restore check”. Select that new entry, verify its directory beneath the list, then open Designer from that entry.
steps.why: Loading replaces the selected target’s content; a new empty target preserves existing work.
steps.expected: A second entry has another name and directory; its Designer is open.

steps.where: New target’s Designer → Administration → Load infobase
steps.action: Confirm that this Designer was launched from the new empty target entry whose directory you checked. If unsure, cancel and return to the startup list; a matching window title is insufficient. Choose Administration → Load infobase and select your .dt. Read the replacement warning and continue only for the new empty target. Wait for completion and the normal restart if prompted.
steps.why: Test whether the dump can actually be restored. The original is not the target.
steps.expected: The new infobase opens after loading and shows the saved training state.

steps.action: Close the restoration target. Open the original and restored infobases in Enterprise mode, one at a time. Compare expected objects and records. Both empty infobases normally have no application sections. Record source, copy name and observation in Nexus.
steps.why: Actual reopening supplements the file and success message.
steps.expected: Both infobases remain independently available; the original is intact and the copy matches the dump state.
